prerequisites: Sufficient knowledge about the functioning of a computer and its peripherals.
Knowledge of a procedural and/or object-oriented programming language.

learning_outcomes.text: Indicate the objectives of an operating system.
Know the minimal hardware support (interrupt mechanism, memory protection, ...) required to execute a modern operating system.
Functionally describe the components of an operating system.
Describe the main algorithms used in the implementation of these components, weigh their pros and cons against each other, and indicate the necessary hardware support.
Make an informed choice between these algorithms based on certain criteria and the available hardware.
Design parallel collaborating programs and provide the necessary synchronization commands.
Compare operating systems with each other and provide informed advice.
Understand the implementation of a simple educational operating system.
Make simple adjustments and extensions to a simple educational operating system.
Be able to work at a low level in the C programming language, including memory manipulation.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: What is an operating system? Evolution of operating systems. Different types of operating systems.
General structure of an operating program: Components, services, system calls, system programs, structure, virtual machines, design and development, installation.
Processes: Concept, process scheduling, operations on processes, cooperating processes, threads, interprocess communication.
Threads: concepts, multithreading models, threading issues.
CPU scheduling: Concepts, criteria, algorithms, evaluation.
Process synchronization: Background, critical section problem, synchronization HW, semaphores, classic synchronization problems, critical regions, monitors.
Deadlocks: characterization, methods for handling deadlocks: prevention, avoidance, detection and recovery.
Memory management: Background, logical and physical address space, swapping, contiguous allocation, paging, segmentation, paged segmentation.
Virtual memory: Background, demand paging, performance, page replacement, replacement algorithms, frame allocation, thrashing.
File system: File, access methods, directory structure, protection, consistency.
Implementation of a file system: File system structure, allocation methods, free space management, directory implementation, efficiency and performance, recovery procedures.
Secondary storage management: Disk structure, disk scheduling, disk management, swap-space management, reliability, stable storage.
I/O systems: I/O hardware, I/O interface, interrupts, kernel I/O subsystem.
Protection: Objectives, protection domain, access matrix, access matrix implementation, revocation of access rights, capability-based systems, language-based protection.
Security: Security problem, causes, security policy, "intentional" threats, authentication, measures, cryptography.
Case studies: Windows and Linux.
The use of C in low-level kernel code
The use of system calls
The implementation of new system calls
The management of virtual and physical memory
Handling traps (interrupts and exceptions) in the kernel
Process management
Synchronization in the kernel
File systems
assessment_rules: Evaluation consists of continuous assessment for the practicals and a final written exam during the examination period. If the evaluation shows that the student has insufficiently achieved one or more objectives of the course, the overall result may deviate from the weighted average of the components. The final written exam in the third examination period has the same form as the exam in the first examination period. Practicals cannot be made up during the third examination period.
